stem: A nurse manager conducts leadership walkrounds on a patient-care unit. Which approach best supports the safety purpose of these rounds?

options.A: Invite frontline staff to discuss safety concerns and ensure concerns receive structured follow-up.
options.B: Use the rounds only to observe staff silently and avoid discussing problems.
options.C: Collect concerns but avoid follow-up so staff remain independent.
options.D: Limit the rounds to reviewing financial performance with no discussion of patient safety.

rationale: AHRQ describes leadership walkrounds as management visits to clinical areas that engage frontline workers in discussion of safety concerns. Their value depends on meaningful follow-up; concerns raised without response can make the rounds a visibility exercise rather than an effective safety intervention.
educational_objective: Explain how leadership walkrounds should be used to support patient safety.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, PSNet
source_document_title: The Role of Leadership in Improving Safety
source_locator: Leadership walkrounds—engage frontline workers in safety discussions; concerns should receive prompt follow-up
source_claim_supported: Leadership walkrounds engage frontline staff about safety concerns and require follow-up to be meaningful.
correction_summary: Replaced generic 'leader rounding' satisfaction claims with the AHRQ-defined patient-safety function.
audit_findings: Correct option contains both engagement and follow-up.
Other options remove the safety communication function.
Independent second pass found no competing answer.
